findings.title: Document numbering values allocate multi-gigabyte Chicago labels
findings.summary: A small admitted DOCX can set a list start or endnote numStart to 4294967295 with Chicago numbering. The renderer converts that numeric value directly into 1,073,741,824 repeated double-daggers, allocating 3 GiB before subsequent layout and copies. Document suppliers can exhaust a consuming process without a large archive or deep XML.

severity.rationale: Attacker-supplied document input deterministically amplifies a tiny numeric field into gigabytes, threatening process availability. No shared production service is assumed; policy recommends external CPU/memory isolation.
severity.changeConditions: A network-facing shared conversion deployment raises exposure; strict worker memory/time limits constrain the blast radius to a worker.

confidence.rationale: Static source establishes unchecked u32 parsing, direct counter propagation, and unconditional repeat; no runtime or deployment proof is required for the public parser boundary.

codeEvidence.label: Numeric value controls allocation length
codeEvidence.explanation: At u32::MAX, the selected 3-byte mark is repeated 2^30 times with no output budget.

codeEvidence.label: Untrusted list start accepts full u32 range
codeEvidence.explanation: The parsed start feeds NumLevel.start, next_marker and render without a semantic maximum.

codeEvidence.label: Marker formatter runs before label replacement
codeEvidence.explanation: The placeholder path materializes the entire label; layout or output clipping occurs later.

codeEvidence.label: Endnote format and start use the same formatter
codeEvidence.explanation: The endnote numStart/numFmt sibling operation also reaches the unbounded formatter.

rootCause.summary: Numeric numbering parameters are treated as output sizes; chicago_label applies str::repeat without checking the expanded marker byte length.

findings.remediation: Enforce a finite expanded-marker byte budget before allocation for every numeric-format consumer. Refuse or safely fall back when start/counter values exceed format-specific limits; propagate a typed refusal instead of allocating. Cover list starts, startOverride, and endnote numbering.

counterEvidence: src/convert/mod.rs:773-774 admits the input first; src/admission.rs:63-76 bounds archive sizes and XML depth, but no semantic number/output bound exists on this path.
SECURITY.md advises CPU/memory-limited workers; no guarantee against all denial of service is claimed.
limitations: No vulnerability-triggering input or runtime reproduction executed.
validation.summary: Independently validated from public PDF entry through with_layout admission, list start parsing, counter propagation and render/format_num; endnote numStart reaches the same sink. Archive/XML budgets bound input bytes and structure, not numeric expansion.

dataflow.summary: word/numbering.xml w:start (or endnotePr/numStart) -> u32 start -> Numbering counter/endnote counter -> format_num(Chicago,n) -> chicago_label -> str::repeat.

impact.rationale: Process memory exhaustion, OOM termination or prolonged CPU/memory pressure.

likelihood.rationale: Direct deterministic numeric-to-allocation path under default parsing; exploitation depends on victim processing the document.

reachability.summary: Public docx_to_pdf[_with/_report] accepts caller-provided bytes, admits the package, loads numbering, and formats the first matching numbered paragraph; a normal %1 placeholder is sufficient.
reachability.attacker: Supplier of a DOCX processed by another user's application
preconditions: Victim converts or renders attacker-controlled DOCX containing an active Chicago numbered paragraph or endnote.
No trusted configuration changes, large payload, or prior host access are needed.

attackPath.summary: Document author crosses the untrusted DOCX-to-renderer boundary using small numeric attributes to consume host memory.

remediationTests: Use deterministic formatter tests at the maximum accepted marker size and just beyond it, including u32::MAX, without allocating the oversized string.
Add integration fixtures with small Chicago list starts/startOverride and endnote numStart that exceed the output budget; assert bounded refusal.

candidate.title: Unbounded numbering level triggers billions of iterations or counter insertions
candidate.originalEvidence: Baseline: direct ilvl u32 at 12711-12714 feeds resolve_ilvl 5518-5532 looping 0..ilvl in reverse, so ilvl=4294967294 with only normal level 0 performs ~4B hash lookups. If malicious numbering defines that high ilvl, next_marker loops 0..resolved inserting billions of HashMap counters (5610-5627). No value range validation seen.

candidate.title: Predictable plan staging follows symlinks
candidate.originalEvidence: Investigator: recordPlan constructs .<plan basename>.<process.pid>.partial then fs.writeFileSync without exclusive/no-follow flags (lines 423-425), allowing a local attacker able to populate plan directory to pre-place a symlink and truncate a victim before rename. Independently reachable from plan-recording (--plan plus operation flags). Local-directory-write precondition; no document-only path escape found.

candidate.title: Unbounded HTML colspan expansion
candidate.originalEvidence: Baseline: src/convert/altchunk.rs:563-566 parses HTML td colspan as unrestricted usize; end_table computes cols as sum spans (469-475), emits one gridCol per col (489-490). HTML td colspan="18446744073709551615" can drive unbounded string allocation; mod.rs:773 admits original archive, then 790-793 expands HTML with no output budget.
